stem.text: Let f be a continuous function with \( f(3) = 1 \), \( f(6) = -2 \), \( f(9) = 4 \). Let \( g(x) = \int_{2 x}^{x^{2}} f(t) \, dt \). Find the value of \( g'\left(3\right) \).

worked_solution.text: Split the integral at any constant k in the domain of the integrand: \( g(x) = \int_{k}^{x^{2}} f(t) \, dt - \int_{k}^{2 x} f(t) \, dt \), and apply the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus to each piece.
With the chain rule, \( g'(x) = f\left(x^{2}\right) \cdot 2 x - f\left(2 x\right) \cdot 2 \).
At \( x = 3 \): the limits are \( 9 \) and \( 6 \), with derivatives \( 6 \) and \( 2 \), and \( f\left(9\right) = 4 \), \( f\left(6\right) = -2 \).

distractor_derivations.A: f(upper) - f(lower) with both chain rule factors left off
distractor_derivations.C: integrand evaluated at x = 3 instead of at the two limits
distractor_derivations.D: lower limit term added instead of subtracted
